faqs.question: What large-component machining capability does Dhruv EPC have?
faqs.answer: The works holds floor-type boring mills, vertical turning lathes and horizontal lathes capable of machining components up to approximately Ø 4,000 mm — covering tube-sheets, vessel shells, large flanges and nozzle forgings.

faqs.question: Which tolerances can you hold on tube-sheet drilling?
faqs.answer: Tube-sheet drilling and boring is carried out to TEMA tolerances for heat exchanger assembly; the specific tolerance class (R, C or B) is confirmed at enquiry stage against the thermal designer's requirements.

faqs.question: Can you machine exotic alloys such as duplex stainless or high-nickel alloys?
faqs.answer: Yes — the machining shop handles carbon steel, low alloy steel, austenitic stainless steel, duplex stainless steel and high-nickel alloys; tooling and cutting parameters are selected for each material group.

faqs.question: What flange face finishes can you produce?
faqs.answer: Raised-face, flat-face and ring-type-joint (RTJ) grooves to ASME B16.5 and ASME B16.47 Series A and B finish requirements — serrated concentric or phonographic finish per ASME specification.

faqs.question: How does in-house machining benefit pressure vessel fabrication timescales?
faqs.answer: In-house machining at the same Manjusar GIDC site eliminates subcontract transport and schedule risk — tube-sheets, nozzle flanges and shell ends are machined and fit-checked against the vessel without leaving the works.
